items.name: Privacy-preserving information stewardship
items.definition: Enable legitimate, useful sharing of personal or institutional information while limiting collection, secondary use, retention and exposure.
guardrails: Privacy law varies by government and sector.
No surveillance authority follows from modeling data exchange.

items.name: Essential-service continuity and recovery
items.definition: Sustain or restore critical services that people depend on across organizational disruption, infrastructure faults and malicious digital activity.
guardrails: Service availability must reflect actual human need, not just IT uptime.
Emergency response does not create permanent extraordinary power.

items.name: Lifelong skill and workforce development
items.definition: Make durable learning, professional development and transferable competencies possible throughout changing technologies, careers and individual circumstances.
guardrails: Avoid conflating training volume with learning.
Respect State and local education governance and learner choice.

items.name: Independent evidence and outcome measurement
items.definition: Publish transparent, reliable and privacy-respecting evidence that can test national outcomes, institutional performance claims and unforeseen harms.
guardrails: Do not substitute output proxies for citizen benefit.
Disclose representativeness, uncertainty and measurement incentives.

items.name: Transparent public finance and stewardship
items.definition: Evaluate how public revenue, appropriation, debt, investment and economic sustainability interact with essential services and long-term public outcomes.
guardrails: Modeling a fiscal concept does not create taxing or spending authority.
Preserve distinct roles of Congress, Treasury, Federal Reserve and States.

items.name: Accessible participation and meaningful remedies
items.definition: Make services and institutions practically reachable for people and provide fair ways to challenge harmful decisions or errors.
guardrails: Procedural rights depend on applicable law; avoid inventing entitlements.
No automated denial without proportionate review pathways.

items.name: Resilient infrastructure and productive supply networks
items.definition: Support adaptable transportation, energy, communications, clinical supply and industrial capacity with safe recovery from common shocks.
guardrails: Do not assume central governmental ownership or direction.
Assess costs, geography and dependencies rather than output counts alone.

items.name: Secure identity, verification and restoration
items.definition: Protect identities and the integrity of access/transactions while enabling correction, recovery and lawful privacy or anonymity.
guardrails: No mandatory universal biometric or digital ID is implied.
Identity assurance must not unnecessarily exclude individuals.
